BPM Analytics projects sales from retail on wheels will grow to $30 billion worldwide by 2030.

phys.org/news/2026-11-microbes-earth-ant.title: Microbes at the end of the Earth: Antarctica's hidden biodiversity
phys.org/news/2026-11-microbes-earth-ant.excerpt: When we think about Antarctica, many people imagine penguins, seals and whales. However, the majority of Antarctica's scientific wonders cannot be seen without a microscope. These microbial communities form the foundation of Antarctic ecosystems yet remain largely invisible to most visitors.

phys.org/news/2026-11-gas-wound-infectio.title: Gas inside us could fight wound infections, moth study shows
phys.org/news/2026-11-gas-wound-infectio.excerpt: A gas naturally produced by our own bodies could one day help treat skin and wound infections, potentially offering a new approach alongside conventional antibiotics.

phys.org/news/2026-11-captures-northeast.title: Improved snow model captures Northeast's winter thaws and runoff more accurately
phys.org/news/2026-11-captures-northeast.excerpt: Mountain snow in the Northeast is different. The region's milder, more humid mountain climate shapes winter conditions that are different from those of the western United States. Yet, snow models don't always capture those differences.

phys.org/news/2026-10-analysis-inca-mumm.title: Analysis of Inca mummies identifies the drugs used in their most important sacrificial ritual
phys.org/news/2026-10-analysis-inca-mumm.excerpt: Archaeologists have performed toxicological analysis on the mummified remains of people sacrificed at mountain shrines across the Inca Empire, revealing the psychoactive substances they consumed before their deaths.

phys.org/news/2026-11-telltale-furrows-b.title: Telltale furrows: What the Baltic Sea seafloor reveals about bottom trawling
phys.org/news/2026-11-telltale-furrows-b.excerpt: To what extent does bottom trawling impact the seafloor of the Baltic Sea—and how quickly does it recover? Two new studies from the Leibniz Institute for Baltic Sea Research Warnemünde (IOW) show that the marks on the seafloor provide a much clearer picture of the actual impact than vessel position data alone. Using high-resolution echo sounder measurements and AI, the researchers reveal previously insufficiently recorded impacts and also document surprisingly rapid changes of the seafloor condition. Furthermore, they found strong indications of fishing violations in a marine protected area. The study results were published in the journals Ecological Informatics and Anthropocene.

phys.org/news/2026-11-stem-cells-deep-se.title: Stem cells in deep sleep may point to a secret reserve for lifelong blood renewal
phys.org/news/2026-11-stem-cells-deep-se.excerpt: Researchers at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) and the HI-STEM Stem Cell Institute have discovered a group of particularly long-lived blood stem cells in mice. These cells remain in a dormant state for an exceptionally long time while retaining their ability to generate new blood cells. This newly discovered cell population may be responsible for sustaining blood regeneration and immune defense throughout a mouse's entire life.

phys.org/news/2026-11-reproductive-evolu.title: How competing reproductive needs shaped the evolution of liverworts
phys.org/news/2026-11-reproductive-evolu.excerpt: Liverworts reproduce through a life cycle involving two distinct stages. First, sperm fertilize eggs in the presence of water, producing embryos that develop into spore-producing structures called sporophytes. These structures then produce spores that can disperse and grow into new liverwort plants.

phys.org/news/2026-11-arctic-roots-play-.title: Arctic plant roots may play key role in climate change
phys.org/news/2026-11-arctic-roots-play-.excerpt: A new review involving researchers at Umeå University has revealed the critical role that plant roots play in shaping how Arctic tundra ecosystems respond to climate change. The paper, recently published in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, highlights how processes occurring beneath the soil surface could help scientists better understand how one of the fastest-changing ecosystems on Earth will influence the future climate.

phys.org/news/2026-11-optical-illusions-.title: Plants may experience 'optical illusions' that affect their direction of growth
phys.org/news/2026-11-optical-illusions-.excerpt: A new study from Tel Aviv University reveals how plants, despite having neither a brain nor a nervous system, integrate light coming from multiple directions to determine where to grow. The researchers show how this process emerges from local sensing across the stem, without the need for centralized information processing.

phys.org/news/2026-11-canada-infrastruct.title: Canada can develop infrastructure and protect biodiversity
phys.org/news/2026-11-canada-infrastruct.excerpt: Nearly 200 countries recently came together in Armenia for the 2026 United Nations Biodiversity Conference to review progress toward halting and reversing biodiversity loss. Many of these governments will soon convene again in Turkey to discuss efforts to tackle climate change at COP31.

phys.org/news/2026-11-deep-sea-mussels-t.title: Deep-sea mussels trade tidal rhythms for a 24-hour cycle in the lab
phys.org/news/2026-11-deep-sea-mussels-t.excerpt: Hydrothermal vents lie in perpetual darkness in the depths of the ocean, yet the cells of the vent mussel Bathymodiolus azoricus, which lives 1,700 meters (5,600 feet) below the surface, follow a 24-hour rhythm in the laboratory.

phys.org/news/2026-11-attention-nature.h.title: To restore attention, reach out to nature
phys.org/news/2026-11-attention-nature.h.excerpt: The world is a far louder and more distracting place than when humans first evolved. But there's increasing evidence that experiencing nature can help restore attention lost to modern distractions, known as "directed attention fatigue."

phys.org/news/2026-11-impact-deep-sea-se.title: Impact of deep-sea mining on seafloor ecosystem still evident 44 years later
phys.org/news/2026-11-impact-deep-sea-se.excerpt: Little is known about the long-term effects of deep-sea mining on the organic matter that supports life on the seafloor. However, as interest in mining the deep sea for rare metals grows, there is concern that disturbing the seabed could affect the ecosystems of the deep ocean.

phys.org/news/2026-11-magnetic-nanocompo.title: Magnetic nanocomposites could help shrink the components that power computer chips
phys.org/news/2026-11-magnetic-nanocompo.excerpt: When you think about making computer chips better, you probably think about transistors. My colleagues and I focused on a less visible part of the problem: the components that deliver power to those transistors. A chip needs more than electricity. It needs electricity supplied at the right voltage, with fluctuations kept under control. Making the hardware that does this smaller is an important challenge—and one that led my colleagues and me to build tiny magnetic devices called stripline microinductors.

phys.org/news/2026-11-solvable-reveals-m.title: Exactly solvable model reveals how trapped light can create magnetic order in one-dimensional spin chains
phys.org/news/2026-11-solvable-reveals-m.excerpt: A research team wanted to better understand how the forces between particles inside a material change. They discovered that by confining one-dimensional classical spin chains inside a mirror box cavity with light, they could force these magnetic particles to organize and undergo a phase transition. Their work provides the simplest exactly solvable examples showing that light can create new phase transitions with materials.

phys.org/news/2026-11-european-flounder-.title: European flounder can complete whole life cycle in freshwater
phys.org/news/2026-11-european-flounder-.excerpt: Most flounders sampled in Lake Pulmanki in northern Finland had spent their entire lives in freshwater. The study provides the first evidence of the species living entirely in freshwater. The work is published in Evolution.

phys.org/news/2026-11-industrialization-.title: Industrialization reshapes gut microbes, from bacterial communities to their DNA, studies find
phys.org/news/2026-11-industrialization-.excerpt: The totality of bacteria, viruses and fungi that exist in and on a multicellular organism forms its natural microbiome. The interactions between the body and these microorganisms significantly influence the host organism's functions and health. Among other things, researchers have shown that the microbiome plays an important role in defense against pathogens. On the other hand, they suspect that imbalances in the microbiome's composition are linked to the development of so-called environmental diseases, such as chronic inflammation.

phys.org/news/2026-11-fema-zone-home-nei.title: Not in a FEMA flood zone? Your home could still be at risk—and you could suffer more than your neighbor
phys.org/news/2026-11-fema-zone-home-nei.excerpt: If your home isn't in a federally designated flood zone, flooding might seem like someone else's problem. No one requires you to buy flood insurance, and the map suggests you're in the clear. But reality may be very different.

phys.org/news/2026-11-overfertilizing-fi.title: Are we overfertilizing our fields? Researchers challenge conventional soil testing
phys.org/news/2026-11-overfertilizing-fi.excerpt: A new study led by Dr. Shikma Zaarur of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, in collaboration with Dr. Ran Erel of the Agricultural Research Organization–Volcani Institute, reveals that agricultural soils may contain a substantial unaccounted-for reservoir of potassium, an essential nutrient for plant growth, that is largely overlooked by conventional soil testing methods. The findings could pave the way for more precise fertilizer recommendations, potentially reducing unnecessary fertilizer use while supporting sustainable agricultural production.

phys.org/news/2026-11-molecular-dinitrog.title: Molecular dinitrogen anions pave the way for low-temperature ammonia synthesis
phys.org/news/2026-11-molecular-dinitrog.excerpt: While ammonia (NH₃) is best known for its role in fertilizer production, it is attracting attention as a carbon-free hydrogen carrier, potentially offering a practical way to store and transport clean fuel. Despite this promise, NH₃ synthesis still depends on high-temperature, high-pressure processes that are difficult to scale up sustainably. The reason behind this is the extremely strong bond between nitrogen atoms in nitrogen gas (N₂), which requires a lot of energy to break.

phys.org/news/2026-11-science-gain-respe.title: According to science, you may be more likely to gain respect and status by helping others
phys.org/news/2026-11-science-gain-respe.excerpt: Human intelligence is still a bit of an enigma. Researchers have some ideas about why advanced intelligence evolved in humans, but they have not come to a conclusive answer. One prominent idea is that intelligence serves a social function. In their new study, a group of researchers led by Jonathan Egeland reports additional evidence supporting this idea. According to their research, published in the journal Evolution and Human Behavior, greater intelligence seems to garner more respect, but only when it's applied to tasks that help others.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261102.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261102.excerpt: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261101.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261101.excerpt: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261031.title: Large Hadron Collider reveals evidence of Big Bang matter in surprisingly small collisions
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261031.excerpt: Scientists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have uncovered compelling new evidence that even relatively small atomic collisions can recreate the extraordinary state of matter that filled the universe moments after the Big Bang. Known as quark-gluon plasma, this exotic substance forms at temperatures more than 100,000 times hotter than the center of the Sun, causing ordinary particles to break apart into their fundamental building blocks.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261031.title: Scientists reverse liver cell aging and cut Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261031.excerpt: A surprising discovery suggests that rejuvenating the liver could help protect against Alzheimer’s disease and heart disease. USC researchers found that an experimental drug restored aging liver cells in rats, cutting levels of an Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half and bringing bad cholesterol down to youthful levels. The treatment also revived a previously unknown communication system that helps liver cells remove harmful substances from the bloodstream.

livescience.com/animals/dinosaurs/traces.title: Traces of ancient blood found in 115 million-year-old dinosaur fossil, new study claims
livescience.com/animals/dinosaurs/traces.excerpt: Chemical signatures found in a Brazilian dinosaur bone may be preserved red blood cells, a new study suggests, but not all experts agree.

insideclimatenews.org/news/02112026/beef.title: ‘Bookkeeping Trick’ and Fuzzy Math Conceal the Climate Impacts of Beef, Researchers Say
insideclimatenews.org/news/02112026/beef.excerpt: Climate negotiators head to Turkey next month for the United Nations annual climate summit, just two months after an alarming U.N. report said the world has a vanishing chance of limiting global warming to safe levels. The report’s projections will likely ripple through discussions at the event, known as the Conference of the Parties or […]

statnews.com/2026/11/02/bird-flu-washing.title: Washington state resident dies from bird flu following exposure to infected cattle
statnews.com/2026/11/02/bird-flu-washing.excerpt: A person in Washington state has died from complications of the bird flu, the first such U.S. death in a year.

space.com/entertainment/space-books/new-.title: New 'Star Trek: The Original Voyages' book traces the stellar legacy of the bold sci-fi brand
space.com/entertainment/space-books/new-.excerpt: Keep the 60th anniversary party going with this visual salute to the series that launched a legacy

space.com/stargazing/skywatching-kit/vil.title: Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.8 II EVO FE (APO) lens review — how good is this budget lens for astrophotography?
space.com/stargazing/skywatching-kit/vil.excerpt: The Viltrox AF 35mm f/1.8 II FE (APO) is an inexpensive prime that works well for astrophotography thanks to its focal length and maximum aperture.

astronomy.com/whats-launching-this-week/.title: South Korea eyes rocket debut and China lines up four launches
astronomy.com/whats-launching-this-week/.excerpt: Rocket launches this week On Monday, Nov. 2, Rocket Lab launched The Sea God Surveys on an Electron rocket from its Launch Complex 1 on New Zealand’s Māhia Peninsula at 11:41 a.m. EST. Aboard was a QPS-SAR satellite for private Japanese company iQPS It marked Electron’s 10th flight for iQPS. The company is building out Continue reading "South Korea eyes rocket debut and China lines up four launches" The post South Korea eyes rocket debut and China lines up four launches appeared first on Astronomy Magazine .

universetoday.com/articles/the-vera-rubi.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
universetoday.com/articles/the-vera-rubi.excerpt: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of these satellites, our understanding of galaxy growth, and the role dark matter plays in it, will improve.

universetoday.com/articles/the-jwst-may-.title: The JWST May Have Found Where Heavy Black Hole Seeds Formed
universetoday.com/articles/the-jwst-may-.excerpt: Astrophysicists think that black holes grow through a hierarchical merger framework. But the elusive Intermediate Mass Black Holes are the missing link between stellar mass black holes, and the gargantuan supermassive black holes like the one at the center of the Milky Way. The JWST may have found the ancient sources of IMBH heavy seeds: young massive clusters in the high-redshift Universe.

universetoday.com/articles/researchers-m.title: Researchers May Have Solved a Puzzling Contradiction in the Ryugu Sample
universetoday.com/articles/researchers-m.excerpt: Samples from the asteroid Ryugu, and from carbonaceous chondrites that have crashed on Earth, present an apparent contradiction. Their fine-grained matrices have widely varied compositions of their clay-like minerals. That suggests that there were widely different aqueous environments in the same parent bodies, which seems unlikely. But new research may have solved that contradiction.

9.headline: Ultracold Rubidium Atoms Mimic Schwinger Pair Production
9.summary: Researchers used an optical lattice of ultracold rubidium atoms to simulate the elusive Schwinger effect, revealing how mass and field strength control pair creation.
highlights: Ultracold rubidium atoms were arranged in a one‑dimensional optical lattice to represent a false vacuum
Tuning the simulated particle mass and background electric field altered the observed pair‑production rate
Quantum gas microscope imaging captured real‑time dynamics of the simulated particle‑antiparticle creation

7.headline: Delayed Rise of Lyman Continuum Escape in Bursty High‑Redshift Galaxies
7.summary: Simulations show that Lyman continuum escape fractions peak about 16 Myr after star‑formation bursts, especially in massive early galaxies.
highlights: Typical LyC escape lag is ~16 Myr with peak correlations of 0.4‑0.6 in massive haloes
Delay scales as M★⁻⁰·¹⁹ and Mhalo⁻⁰·²⁷, lengthening for lower‑mass systems
Hα‑to‑UV luminosity ratio retains a delayed link to LyC escape, offering an observable tracer

15.headline: Astrolabe Surrogate Generates Full‑Resolution Cosmology Simulations via Flow Matching
15.summary: Astrolabe uses a flow‑matching transformer to emulate particle‑level cosmology, delivering accurate large‑scale structure without voxel resolution limits.
highlights: Acts directly on 6N phase‑space coordinates of individual particles
Employs a hybrid transformer where each particle cross‑attends to multiscale field tokens
Matches physical flow using approximate COLA coordinates, preserving momentum and mass
Reproduces power spectra, halo mass functions, velocity and density profiles in Lambda‑CDM tests
Generalizes to dark‑acoustic oscillation initial conditions and scales to TNG50‑3‑dark size

3.headline: Vienna Researchers Unveil First Self-Stabilizing Thorium‑229 Nuclear Clock
3.summary: A team at TU Wien built a self‑stabilizing nuclear clock using thorium‑229 nuclei, achieving a precision of one‑second error over 30 million years.
highlights: The clock uses a laser‑driven transition in thorium‑229 nuclei to lock its frequency
It operates autonomously for over 24 hours without an external atomic reference
Measured relative precision reaches 10⁻¹⁵, far surpassing typical atomic clocks

8.headline: Rare FN1 Mutation Shields APOE ε4 Carriers from Alzheimer’s Brain Damage
8.summary: Scientists identified a protective FN1 mutation that limits fibrotic buildup around brain vessels, preserving blood‑brain barrier integrity in APOE ε4 carriers into their 80s.
highlights: APOE ε4 drives excess fibronectin accumulation around cerebral blood vessels
A rare FN1 mutation reduces fibronectin deposition and prevents barrier leakage
Single‑cell and spatial analyses confirmed the mechanism in mouse, zebrafish, and human tissue
Findings published in Nature Aging suggest new therapeutic targets for early Alzheimer’s intervention

microblazar_discovery.headline: Astronomers Spot First Microblazar Inside Milky Way Pointing Toward Earth
microblazar_discovery.summary: A tiny blazar, IR 18293‑0941, has been identified in our galaxy, offering a fast‑forward view of jet physics and a possible source of ultrahigh‑energy particles.
highlights: IRAS 18293‑0941 exhibits a one‑sided bright radio jet, the hallmark of a blazar.
Multi‑wavelength data from three observatories confirmed the source lies within the Milky Way.
The jet’s opposite‑directed shock may power the nearby ultrahigh‑energy particle hotspot.
The findings are detailed in a forthcoming Astronomy & Astrophysics paper after two decades of searching.

early_universe_collider.headline: STAR experiment spots unexpected dip hinting at nuclear matter critical point
early_universe_collider.summary: Physicists at RHIC observed a non‑monotonic dip in transverse‑momentum correlations of gold‑gold collisions, suggesting a possible critical point in nuclear matter.
highlights: Dip in correlation strength deviates from smooth trend across 3–7.7 GeV collisions
Signal reaches 5 σ significance, far beyond statistical fluctuations
Findings published in Physical Review Letters and challenge existing simulation models

focused_light_correlations.headline: Giant Fluctuations in Focused Light Reveal Hidden Correlations in Opaque Media
focused_light_correlations.summary: Researchers found that the enhancement factor’s large fluctuations during wavefront shaping expose long‑range mesoscopic correlations in strongly scattering zinc‑oxide nanoparticle layers.
highlights: Enhancement factor fluctuations can be several times larger than predictions from correlation‑free random‑matrix theory.
Giant fluctuations increase with sample thickness, using fewer than ~200 input channels or even a single output channel.
The effect was demonstrated experimentally with zinc‑oxide nanoparticle layers and validated by numerical simulations.

smile_earth_photos.headline: Smile Satellite Captures Daytime Aurora Over North Pole in Stunning UV Images
smile_earth_photos.summary: First ultraviolet photos from the ESA‑China Smile mission reveal a massive aurora swirling over the sunlit North Pole, offering an unprecedented daylight view of Earth’s magnetic storms.
highlights: Ultraviolet Aurora Imager captured a serpent‑like auroral ring covering about one‑third of Earth’s disc.
Smile orbits 75,000 mi (121,000 km) above the North Pole, allowing up to 45‑hour continuous observations.
The mission, a joint effort of ESA and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, began formal science operations in July 2026.

14.headline: UCLA Study Links Specific Gut Bacteria to Faster Brain Aging in Young Adults
14.summary: A UCLA analysis of nearly 1,500 adults finds that certain gut microbes and their metabolites correlate with an elevated Brain Aging Index and poorer cognition.
highlights: Brain Aging Index derived from resting‑state brain scans predicts memory and mood deficits
Higher BAI associates with distinct gut bacteria, fat molecules, a cholesterol‑related compound, and lower estetrol
Study spans three cohorts and is published in eBioMedicine

11.headline: JWST Spectroscopy Reveals Common Mini‑Quenched Galaxies at z > 4
11.summary: Deep 28‑hour NIRSpec/PRISM observations in the OASIS program find that suppressed, mini‑quenched and lulling galaxies constitute a sizable fraction of early low‑mass galaxies.
highlights: Three mini‑quenched galaxies with log(M/Msun)=8.3‑8.9 lie 1.2‑1.7 dex below the star‑forming main sequence
Five lulling galaxies show weak Balmer emission just above the quenching threshold
Suppressed galaxies represent 29% of the sample at z=4‑5.5, with a number density ≈1.6×10⁻³ Mpc⁻³ dex⁻¹
Photometric estimates overstate star‑formation rates, misclassifying most candidates without spectroscopy

12.headline: Vacuum Metamorphosis Model Beats ΛCDM in Explaining Dark Energy Dynamics
12.summary: A vacuum metamorphosis model with decay fits BAO, supernova and CMB data better than ΛCDM and rivals w₀wₐCDM in precision.
highlights: Vacuum metamorphosis freezes Ricci scalar curvature at a critical value set by a massive scalar field mass.
The resulting phantom equation of state (w < ‑1) transitions to w > ‑1 as vacuum energy decays into light particles.
Fits to current BAO, supernova distances and CMB measurements outperform ΛCDM with the same parameter count.
Provides a physically motivated dark‑energy scenario without invoking explicit matter couplings.

pah_detection_sextansa.headline: JWST Detects Compact PAH Emission in Ultra‑Metal‑Poor Galaxy Sextans A
pah_detection_sextansa.summary: JWST mid‑infrared imaging reveals small, neutral PAH clumps spanning 3–10 pc in the 7 % Solar metallicity galaxy Sextans A, the lowest‑metallicity PAH detection yet.
highlights: PAH emission resolved in clumps of 0.5‑1.5″ (3‑10 pc)
Feature ratios (3.3, 7.7, 11.3 µm) show grains are small and neutral
Compact PAH sites suggest in‑situ growth rather than destruction
Detection pushes PAH observations to 7 % Solar metallicity, the lowest recorded

2610_02301v1.headline: New SMICA Enhancements Boost LiteBIRD’s Quest for Primordial B‑Mode Signal
2610_02301v1.summary: Researchers refined SMICA component separation and added sky‑subset processing, achieving unbiased tensor‑to‑scalar ratio r measurements with uncertainties near 10⁻³ in LiteBIRD simulations.
highlights: SMICA is augmented with effective dust and synchrotron foreground components beyond physical degrees of freedom
The method now operates on independent sky patches to capture local foreground variations
Likelihood‑level marginalization using internally reconstructed templates further reduces bias
Simulations use increasingly complex foreground models d1s1 and d10s5
Recovered tensor‑to‑scalar ratio r reaches statistically unbiased levels with ≈10⁻³ uncertainty

2610_02667v1.headline: Study Shows Cosmic Birefringence Can Distinguish Dark Energy, Dark Matter, Neutrino Asymmetry
2610_02667v1.summary: Researchers calculate the EB power spectrum for neutrino‑asymmetry currents and compare it with axion dark energy and dark matter, finding distinct signatures across multipoles.
highlights: Neutrino‑asymmetry induced EB spectrum is suppressed at low multipoles (ℓ ≲ 20) like dark matter
Dark‑energy‑driven birefringence shows no low‑ℓ suppression, providing a clear discriminator
Large‑scale polarization data from LiteBIRD can separate late‑time dark‑energy effects from early‑time sources
High‑ℓ features altered by neutrino density evolution enable ground‑based experiments such as the Simons Observatory to tell

2610_03148v1.headline: Phase Transition May Hide Twin Stars in Proto-Neutron Star Evolution
2610_03148v1.summary: A study shows that first‑order hadron‑to‑quark transitions in proto‑neutron stars likely prevent observable gravitational twin‑star pairs, especially at high densities.
highlights: First‑order phase transition from hadronic to deconfined quark matter modeled with a parameterizable EOS
Hybrid star branch can appear “in the shadow” of the hadronic branch on the mass‑radius diagram
Gravitational twin stars are only possible without a corresponding baryonic twin
Most twin‑star configurations are ruled out if the transition occurs at large densities

he_neutrinos_dm_phase_transition.headline: Superheavy Dark Matter from First‑Order Phase Transition Links Ultra‑High‑Energy Neutrinos and Gravitational
he_neutrinos_dm_phase_transition.summary: A cosmological first‑order phase transition can produce super‑heavy dark matter that decays into ultra‑high‑energy neutrinos and generates a stochastic gravitational‑wave background.
highlights: Dark matter mass around 4.4×10⁸ GeV matches relic abundance and explains KM3‑230213A neutrino event
Lower dark‑matter masses (<10⁶ GeV) shift neutrino energies into IceCube’s range and move GW peaks to observable frequencies
Predicted GW signal peaks at 10⁴ Hz, with potential detection by Cosmic Explorer, BBO, and DECIGO for lighter dark‑matter

2610_02245v1.headline: Radius‑Augmented Inference Revives JWST Exoplanet Retrievals
2610_02245v1.summary: A new radius‑augmented flow‑matching method restores accurate atmospheric retrievals for real JWST spectra of WASP‑39b and other targets.
highlights: MIRAGE adds planet radius as a latent variable, preventing posterior collapse
Chi‑square per data point improves from 301 to 0.06 for WASP‑39b
Method works across two JWST instruments and three real spectra
Calibration uses nested‑sampling reference with importance sampling and optimal‑transport mapping

optogenetics_nobel_2026.headline: Nobel Prize Honors Optogenetics Pioneers Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel
optogenetics_nobel_2026.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine rewards the discovery of light‑gated ion channels and their transformation into a neuronal switch.
highlights: Channelrhodopsin, first identified in the green alga Chlamydomonas, became the core of optogenetic tools
Karl Deisseroth demonstrated millisecond‑precise control of mouse neurons using light‑activated channels
Optogenetics now links specific brain circuits to behaviours and is entering clinical trials for vision restoration

vaxcyte_phase3.headline: Vaxcyte’s VAX‑31 Hits Phase 3 Endpoints, Targeting 31 Pneumococcal Serotypes
vaxcyte_phase3.summary: The experimental VAX‑31 vaccine met primary goals in a Phase 3 trial, covering 31 serotypes and challenging Pfizer’s Prevnar and Merck’s Capvaxive.
highlights: VAX‑31 achieved primary endpoints in its Phase 3 study
Covers 31 pneumococcal serotypes versus 20‑21 for competitors
Requires two additional trials before regulatory filing
Sets direct competition with Pfizer’s Prevnar and Merck’s Capvaxive

bc200_gene_mobility.headline: Human Brain Gene BC200 Retains Jumping Ability, Found Inside Poxvirus
bc200_gene_mobility.summary: Researchers at Cornell University identified the neuronal gene BC200 as a mobile element that can still transpose within the human genome and even integrate into a poxvirus.
highlights: BC200 originated from a transposon millions of years ago but remains capable of moving within DNA.
The gene is primarily expressed in neurons and low levels in sperm and eggs.
BC200 was discovered embedded in molluscum contagiosum virus, suggesting cross‑species transfer.
Abnormal BC200 expression is linked to tumors and Alzheimer’s disease, raising concerns about its mobility’s role in pathology.

dark_matter_possible_detection.headline: LZ Detector Reports Possible Dark Matter Signal, Higgsino Theory Sparks Debate
dark_matter_possible_detection.summary: On Sept 1 the LUX‑ZEPLIN experiment observed a high‑energy recoil that could be a single dark‑matter particle, reviving supersymmetry’s higgsino candidate.
highlights: LZ saw one high‑energy nuclear recoil with no accompanying low‑energy events.
Higgsino models predict such recoils but face constraints from IceCube neutrino non‑detections.
Alternative dark‑matter candidates, including dark photons, are also being examined by the community.

permafrost_degradation_subsidence.headline: Permafrost Thaw Near Umiujaq Triggers Up to 3.8 m of Ground Subsidence Over Two Decades
permafrost_degradation_subsidence.summary: A 20‑year study (2004‑2024) links rising active‑layer thickness to accelerating land‑surface sinking of up to 3.8 meters near the Indigenous community of Umiujaq, Québec.
highlights: Ground‑based leveling, high‑resolution LiDAR, and UAV photogrammetry recorded cumulative subsidence of up to 3.8 m.
Active‑layer deepening and talik formation coincided with a marked acceleration after the 1992‑2000s warming spike.
The study provides a replicable monitoring framework for ice‑rich permafrost regions worldwide.

phoenix_planet_duplicate.headline: ‘Phoenix’ Planet Detected Around Niobium‑Rich White Dwarf HS 0209+0832
phoenix_planet_duplicate.summary: Astronomers report the first evidence of a second‑generation planet forming from the ashes of a dead star, identified by unusual niobium signatures.
highlights: Niobium levels in HS 0209+0832 are unprecedented for any known white dwarf
The white dwarf shows a 4.4‑day brightness modulation suggesting a close‑orbiting gas giant
The planet’s composition likely reflects s‑process elements forged in the star’s red‑giant phase

galactic_pevatron_penrose_process.headline: Magnetic Penrose Process Could Power PeV Protons Near Milky Way’s Black Hole
galactic_pevatron_penrose_process.summary: A new arXiv study proposes that neutron decay within Sag A’s ergosphere can launch PeV‑energy protons, producing detectable gamma‑ray and neutrino signatures.
highlights: Neutron decay inside the ergosphere of Sag A may boost protons to PeV energies via the Magnetic Penrose Process
Escaping protons would generate a distinctive gamma‑ray spectrum and accompanying high‑energy neutrinos
Future upgrades to HAWC and IceCube could finally observe these multimessenger signals

first_galaxies_simulations.headline: MEGATRON Simulations Bridge JWST Early Galaxies and Milky Way Stellar Fossils
first_galaxies_simulations.summary: Advanced MEGATRON simulations link James Webb Space Telescope observations of infant galaxies with the chemical fingerprints of the Milky Way’s oldest stars.
highlights: MEGATRON tracks gas, radiation, and chemistry from the post‑Big Bang era to Milky Way‑mass galaxies
The simulations reproduce Population III star formation, supernova enrichment, and subsequent galaxy evolution
Results show prior models underestimated intergalactic gas response to stellar radiation
40 million processor‑hour allocation on UK national supercomputers enables unprecedented resolution

quark_gluon_plasma_waves_lhc.headline: Quarks Create Fluid‑Like Waves in Primordial Quark‑Gluon Plasma at CERN
quark_gluon_plasma_waves_lhc.summary: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have directly observed quark‑induced wakes, confirming the early universe’s quark‑gluon plasma behaved as a true liquid.
highlights: Quark wakes detected using Z boson tags in 2,000 events from 13 billion heavy‑ion collisions
Observations match predictions of the MIT hybrid model for a near‑perfect liquid
Study appears in Physics Letters B and was supported by the U.S. Department of Energy

ultrafast_xray_energy_transfer.headline: Ultrafast X‑rays Reveal How Proton‑Coupled Electron Transfer Moves Energy Efficiently
ultrafast_xray_energy_transfer.summary: Researchers used ultrafast X‑ray spectroscopy and scattering at SLAC’s LCLS to capture coordinated electron‑proton and water‑network motions in a ruthenium complex, shedding light on nature’s efficient energy conversion.
highlights: Combined X‑ray absorption (chemRIXS) and scattering (XCS) captured simultaneous electronic and solvent changes
The study focused on a light‑driven proton‑coupled electron transfer (PCET) reaction in a ruthenium‑based molecule
Results were interpreted with time‑dependent density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations

cartilage_regeneration_protein_blockade.headline: Stanford Researchers Block 15‑PGDH to Regrow Knee Cartilage and Halt Osteoarthritis
cartilage_regeneration_protein_blockade.summary: Blocking the age‑linked enzyme 15‑PGDH rejuvenated chondrocytes, thickened hyaline cartilage in old mice and sparked regeneration in human knee tissue.
highlights: 15‑PGDH levels double with age and its inhibition restored cartilage thickness in aged mice
The inhibitor shifted old chondrocyte populations toward a youthful, hyaline‑cartilage phenotype
Treated human cartilage from knee‑replacement patients began producing new articular cartilage

high_temp_superconductor_assumption_coll.headline: Warwick and ESRF Reveal Patchwork Structure in Cuprate Superconductor LESCO
high_temp_superconductor_assumption_coll.summary: Using 3D X‑ray diffraction, researchers discovered that the cuprate LESCO contains two distinct crystal arrangements, overturning a four‑decade‑old uniformity assumption.
highlights: University of Warwick and European Synchrotron Radiation Facility employed 3D X‑ray diffraction to map interior structures
The cuprate LESCO shows two atomic arrangements separated by unusually wide boundaries
The finding challenges the long‑standing belief that high‑temperature cuprates have a uniform crystal lattice

pulse_oximeter_bias_shift.headline: Pulse Oximeters at Johns Hopkins Hospital Shift From Over‑ to Under‑Estimating Blood Oxygen
pulse_oximeter_bias_shift.summary: A five‑year retrospective study at Johns Hopkins Hospital found its pulse oximeters began underestimating oxygen levels in all patients, with larger errors among patients of color.
highlights: Overestimation turned into underestimation across five years of ICU data
Inaccuracies were worse for patients with darker skin tones
Masimo reported no known sensor or software changes to explain the shift

warming_oceans_reshape_plankton.headline: Warming Oceans Reshape Phytoplankton and Zooplankton, Threatening Fish Nutrition
warming_oceans_reshape_plankton.summary: Rising sea temperatures are altering the species composition and abundance of phytoplankton and zooplankton, potentially reducing the nutritional quality of fish stocks.
highlights: AI-driven image analysis speeds plankton monitoring across multiple European sites
Research led by Lauriane Ribas‑Deulofeu at Nord University links plankton shifts to fish food quality
The BioBoost+ network unites eight institutions in seven countries to standardize microplankton AI methods

chip_frequency_comb_atomic_clocks.institution: Various (research team on chip‑based frequency combs)
chip_frequency_comb_atomic_clocks.headline: Chip‑Integrated Optical Frequency Comb Paves Way for Portable Atomic Clocks
chip_frequency_comb_atomic_clocks.summary: A new chip‑scale frequency comb using self‑aligned parametrically‑driven cavity solitons matches tabletop performance while drastically reducing size.
highlights: Joint Quantum Institute and collaborators demonstrated a micro‑resonator comb that self‑aligns frequency lines
The SParCS approach uses two lasers to generate an octave‑spanning comb with strong edge teeth
Portable comb successfully linked optical and microwave frequencies, enabling stable microwave generation for atomic clocks

gutless_worms_symbiosis.institution: Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology
gutless_worms_symbiosis.headline: Gutless marine worms swap bacterial partners like shoppers at a marketplace
gutless_worms_symbiosis.summary: Researchers found that gutless worms regularly exchange bacterial symbionts, adapting to local conditions despite their extreme dependence on microbes.
highlights: Study examined nearly 250 gutless worms across 63 species from 17 ocean locations
Bacterial communities stay consistent within a worm species but differ sharply between species
Worms periodically acquire new symbionts and discard old ones, expanding their metabolic options

pa30_supernova_remnant.institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
pa30_supernova_remnant.headline: Gemini North Images Reveal Pearl‑Like Chains in Unique Supernova Remnant Pa 30
pa30_supernova_remnant.summary: Using the Gemini North telescope, astronomers captured unprecedented detail of Pa 30, showing gas knots each large enough to contain the solar system ten times over.
highlights: Pearl‑like gas knots form chains spanning widths that could fit the solar system ten times over
Pa 30 is the only known Milky Way remnant of a Type Iax supernova with a surviving “zombie” star
The team measured an extremely small transverse kick speed for the central remnant star
Ionized sulfur and doubly ionized oxygen lines revealed ten‑fold more filamentary features than previous images

2610_07183v1.headline: Hierarchical Black Hole Mergers at High Redshift Predicted for LISA and LGWA
2610_07183v1.summary: Early‑Universe simulations show that strong AGN feedback drastically curtails black‑hole merger chains, limiting growth beyond $10^8\,M_{\odot}$ at $z\ge10$.
highlights: NoFB runs produce up to 50 mergers per black hole within a few hundred Myr
FidBH feedback reduces typical mergers to fewer than three per black hole
Merger‑driven growth dominates only when feedback is weak or absent

s301_star_gr_test.headline: S301 Star Offers New Test of Black Hole Geometry with Interferometry
s301_star_gr_test.summary: The newly observed S301 star, orbiting ten times closer than S2, enables unprecedented probes of black‑hole spin and deviations from Schwarzschild using GRAVITY+ precision and kilometre‑baseline interferometry.
highlights: S301 reaches pericentre one‑tenth that of S2, opening a new regime for strong‑gravity tests
Post‑Newtonian secular Hamiltonian framework predicts measurable astrometric deviations over one orbit
GRAVITY+ can detect several non‑rotating geometry deviations and sizable spin‑induced effects
Kilometre‑baseline interferometry could detect much smaller departures from Schwarzschild

frb_host_metallicity_ifu.headline: Integral‑Field Spectroscopy Reveals Metallicity Diversity in Nearby FRB Hosts
frb_host_metallicity_ifu.summary: Using IFU data from LLAMAS and Keck/KCWI, researchers mapped gas‑phase metallicities in five low‑redshift FRB host galaxies, finding significant local variations.
highlights: Metallicity gradients of ≥0.3 dex were measured within four of the five host galaxies
Burst‑site metallicities span 12 + log(O/H) ≈ 8.5–8.9, with one site below 8.5
Global, long‑slit metallicity estimates often miss the true burst‑site values

2610_08318v1.headline: Young Pulsars Reveal Kolmogorov Turbulence in the Ionized Interstellar Medium
2610_08318v1.summary: A new 18‑year timing study of 364 young pulsars shows dispersion measure variations that largely match Kolmogorov turbulence predictions.
highlights: Significant DM variations detected in 89 pulsars using the ultra‑wideband low‑frequency (UWL) receiver
Combined analysis with 21 cm Multibeam data confirms trends in 16 pulsars
Evidence suggests most variations follow a Kolmogorov turbulence spectrum

2610_07975v1.headline: New Sequential Monte Carlo Method Accelerates Neutron-Star EOS Inference for Einstein Telescope
2610_07975v1.summary: A GPU‑accelerated sequential Monte Carlo algorithm can update neutron‑star equation‑of‑state posteriors from thousands of binary mergers in hours, enabling real‑time analysis for the Einstein Telescope.
highlights: Hybrid sequential Monte Carlo combines data and likelihood tempering
Processes ~1500 binary neutron star mergers in a simulated month on a single GPU
Projects a full year of detections could be analyzed in a few days

arxiv_2610_07880v1.headline: Stochastic Bubble Nucleation Shapes Infrared Power Spectrum and Bispectrum in de Sitter Space
arxiv_2610_07880v1.summary: Researchers analyze how random bubble completion times during a first‑order phase transition generate distinctive infrared signatures in the power spectrum and bispectrum of de Sitter cosmology.
highlights: Power spectrum acquires a $k^3$ white‑noise limit after finite‑time cutoff
Bispectrum shows a $k^6$ limit, indicating stronger infrared sensitivity
Thresholds at $H/\beta=1/5$ and $1/8$ mark the onset of tail‑sensitive behavior

nobelprize2026_chemistry_asymmetry.institution: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)
nobelprize2026_chemistry_asymmetry.headline: Nobel Chemistry Prize Recognizes Breakthroughs in Molecular Chirality
nobelprize2026_chemistry_asymmetry.summary: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai earned the 2026 Nobel Chemistry Prize for uncovering reactions that spontaneously generate single‑handed molecules, illuminating the origin of life's chirality.
highlights: Kagan’s 1986 discovery of a nonlinear effect showed tiny catalyst imbalances can amplify product handedness
Soai’s 1995 and 2003 reactions amplified a 2% excess to 87% and then over 99% single‑handed products
The findings enable synthesis of enantiopure drugs, avoiding harmful mirror‑image effects

physicists_found_ghost_superconductivity.headline: Ghostly Pair Density Waves Detected in Uranium Ditelluride After Superconductivity Vanishes
physicists_found_ghost_superconductivity.summary: Physicists at the University of Illinois discovered that pair density waves persist in UTe₂ even after its superconducting phase disappears, hinting at pre‑superconducting electron pairing.
highlights: Pair density waves observed above the 2 K critical temperature in UTe₂
Vector‑magnet scanning tunneling microscopy enabled detection of delicate PDW signatures
Higher‑quality crystals grown by molten‑flux method were crucial for the discovery

nobel2026chem.headline: 2026 Nobel Chemistry Prize Honors Kagan and Soai for Mastering Mirror‑Image Molecules
highlights: Kagan’s 1986 technique steered reactions toward a single chiral outcome
Soai’s 2003 autocatalytic experiment produced only one enantiomer from achiral precursors
Over half of all pharmaceuticals are chiral, and the new methods reduce side‑effects
The discovery reshapes asymmetric organic synthesis and drug manufacturing

el_nino_forest_drought.headline: El Niño‑Driven Drought and Heat Signal New Normal for Tropical Forests
el_nino_forest_drought.summary: During the 2023‑2024 El Niño, about 75 % of tropical forests faced six months of unprecedented drought and heat, foreshadowing a climate‑driven new normal.
highlights: 75 % of global tropical forest area experienced at least six months of simultaneous drought and heat in 2023‑2024.
Models project a nine‑fold increase in severe Amazon drought likelihood by 2100 under high‑emission scenarios.
Combined satellite data and 24 climate models show extreme heat events becoming six times more likely across tropics even with

webb_atmosphere_lava_world.headline: Webb Detects Atmosphere on Scorching Lava World HD 3167 b
webb_atmosphere_lava_world.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope reveals that the ultra‑short‑period super‑Earth HD 3167 b retains a surprisingly cool atmosphere despite orbiting its star every 24 hours.
highlights: Atmosphere inferred from mid‑infrared secondary‑eclipse measurements
HD 3167 b is the coolest lava world yet found with atmospheric evidence
Study published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters (2026)

amazonozone2026.headline: Amazon Wildfires Produce Ozone That Cuts Forest Carbon Uptake by One‑Quarter
amazonozone2026.summary: Ground‑level ozone from Amazon fires reduces surviving trees’ CO₂ absorption by roughly 24 % of the emissions released by the fires themselves.
highlights: Fire‑derived ozone cuts Amazon carbon uptake by an amount equivalent to about a quarter of fire‑released CO₂
The effect peaks during severe droughts linked to El Niño events
Researchers used three decades of observations and a global vegetation model to quantify the hidden loss

phoenix_planet.headline: Astronomers Discover Phoenix Planet Formed from Dead Star’s Ashes
phoenix_planet.summary: A Jupiter‑sized second‑generation planet orbiting white dwarf HS 0209+0832 was identified by transit dips and heavy‑element signatures, marking a first around a zombie star.
highlights: Planet size comparable to Jupiter with a 4.4‑day orbit
Transit dips reveal the planet repeatedly passes in front of the white dwarf
Spectra show unusual heavy elements zinc, copper and niobium
Discovery made using Hubble Space Telescope’s upgraded instruments
First phoenix‑type planet observed around a white dwarf

radio_galaxy_12_5b_ly.headline: Record-Breaking Radio Galaxy TXS 2354+015 Shines from 12.5 Billion Light‑Years Ago
radio_galaxy_12_5b_ly.summary: Astronomers have identified TXS 2354+015 at redshift 4.946, making it the most powerful known radio galaxy from the early universe.
highlights: TXS 2354+015’s intrinsic radio power at 500 MHz surpasses all previously known high‑z radio galaxies.
The galaxy lies at redshift 4.946, when the universe was about 1.2 billion years old.
Its host mass is estimated near 2 trillion solar masses, one of the most massive early galaxies.
Discovered via optical dropout technique, it evaded traditional ultra‑steep‑spectrum radio searches.
The study, led by Barbara Balmaverde (INAF Turin), combines Subaru HSC data with TGSS and VLASS catalogs (arXiv preprint Sep 23).

jwst_extreme_debris_disks_2026_10_07.headline: Webb Telescope Reveals Mars‑Sized Worlds Colliding in Young Star Systems
jwst_extreme_debris_disks_2026_10_07.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers studied 21 extreme debris disks around young stars, uncovering dust signatures that indicate violent collisions between Mars‑sized planetary bodies.
highlights: Only about 1% of young stars exhibit extreme debris disks, making them rare laboratories for studying planetary impacts.
Silica‑rich disks, found around stars younger than 300 million years, point to high‑energy collisions between Mars‑sized bodies.
Silica‑poor disks, spanning a wider age range, suggest lower‑energy impacts such as grazing Moon‑sized collisions.
The study combines new Webb observations with archival Spitzer data to characterize 21 disks, the largest sample to date.

levitating_glass_entanglement.headline: Room‑Temperature Entanglement Achieved Between Levitating Glass Sphere and Light
levitating_glass_entanglement.summary: Physicists have entangled the motion of a 100‑nm glass sphere with light at room temperature, using dual‑laser optical tweezers in a near‑vacuum.
highlights: The 100‑nm glass sphere was levitated in an optical tweezer between two mirrors.
Two lasers of slightly different colors cooled the sphere and generated entanglement simultaneously.
Measured correlations exceeded the entanglement threshold despite the experiment being at room temperature.

nuclear_clocks.headline: First Nuclear Clocks Tick Using Thorium‑229 Reach Unprecedented Precision
nuclear_clocks.summary: Two teams have built working nuclear clocks based on thorium‑229 transitions in CaF2 crystals, achieving fractional instability down to 5 × 10⁻¹³ /√τ.
highlights: Thorium‑229 nuclear transition excited with narrow‑linewidth UV lasers at 148.4 nm
Clock stability of 5 × 10⁻¹³ /√τ surpasses the PTB‑TU Wien device’s 3 × 10⁻¹² /√τ
Devices demonstrated searches for ultralight scalar dark‑matter couplings

p2x7_brain_inflammation_target.headline: Targeting P2X7 Receptor Slashes Brain Inflammation Linked to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s
p2x7_brain_inflammation_target.summary: Blocking the P2X7 receptor dramatically reduces cytokine release in human brain tissue, offering a repurposable drug target for Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, TBI and psychiatric disorders.
highlights: P2X7 antagonism cut IL‑1β release in live human brain slices
Monocyte‑derived microglia used to model human neuroinflammation
Findings replicated in neurosurgical tissue, supporting translational relevance
Potential to repurpose existing CNS‑penetrant drugs for multiple disorders

2610_09748v1.headline: Neutrino Current May Explain Cosmic Birefringence and Helium-4 Anomalies
2610_09748v1.summary: A new study links isotropic cosmic birefringence to a large lepton asymmetry via a Chern‑Simons coupling between the neutrino current and photons.
highlights: First analysis of anisotropic birefringence sourced by lepton-number isocurvature fluctuations on large scales.
On small scales, gravitational effects dominate over axion‑like particle (ALP) scenarios.
A large lepton asymmetry from the Affleck‑Dine mechanism can reproduce the observed isotropic birefringence.
The model may connect to low helium‑4 abundances reported by Subaru EMPRESS and ACT.

nanograv_15yr_fdmodel.headline: Legendre Models Sharpen Pulsar Timing, Cutting Profile‑Evolution Errors by Up to 85%
nanograv_15yr_fdmodel.summary: New Legendre‑based profile‑evolution formulas reduce timing‑delay residuals up to 85% and lower dispersion‑measure bias, improving nanohertz gravitational‑wave searches.
highlights: Legendre polynomial expansion (LIFD) predicts delays far closer to true profile evolution than traditional FD log‑polynomial
Residual timing offset improves by as much as 85% in simulated data when using LIFD.
FD‑based models overestimate injected DM by 0.013 pc cm⁻³, while LIFD reduces the error to 0.0002 pc cm⁻³.

arxiv_2610_08903v1.headline: Strongly‑Lensed Superluminous Supernova at z = 2.0155 Reveals Extreme Stellar Death and Galaxy Feedback
arxiv_2610_08903v1.summary: Astronomers used Keck‑II/KCWI spectroscopy and Pan‑STARRS photometry to study the highly magnified SLSN 2025wny, finding a magnetar engine and powerful outflows at cosmic noon.
highlights: Rest‑frame UV spectra obtained 11–61 days after peak with Keck‑II/KCWI
Magnification of the brightest image measured at μ_A = 19.4 ± 1.6, exceeding model predictions
Magnetar spin period P_spin = 4.1^{+0.7}_{-1.0} ms and field B_⊥ ≈ 2.4×10^{14} G fit the early light curve

arxiv_2610_08947v1.headline: SPT-3G Detects Record‑High Clustering of tSZ‑Selected Galaxy Clusters
arxiv_2610_08947v1.summary: A five‑year SPT‑3G survey measured galaxy‑cluster clustering at 12.8σ, yielding a halo bias of 5.30±0.24 and tightening mass‑observable constraints.
highlights: Cluster clustering detected at 12.8σ, the strongest tSZ‑selected signal to date
Halo bias measured as bₕ = 5.30±0.24 for clusters spanning 0.25 < z < 1.1
Normalization of the mass‑observable relation constrained to lnAₛz = 0.43⁺⁰·¹⁷₋₀·₂¹

arxiv_2610_08931v1.headline: Stellar Feedback Sparks Early Hot Corona Around Milky Way‑type Galaxies
arxiv_2610_08931v1.summary: Simulations show that stellar feedback can generate a hot circumgalactic medium as early as redshift 3, far earlier than accretion‑shock models predict.
highlights: Stellar feedback drives hot CGM formation at $z\approx3$, reaching virial temperatures.
Feedback‑free runs fail to produce comparable CGM temperatures before $z\lesssim1$.
Hot corona emergence triggers CGM virialisation within ≤0.5 Gyr, often outside‑in.
The apparent evolution of the corona is largely due to “pseudo‑evolution” of $R_{\mathrm{vir}}$.

arxiv_2610_08999v1.headline: Euclid Survey Reveals Shifting Quenching Mechanisms Across Cosmic Time
arxiv_2610_08999v1.summary: Analysis of Euclid Q1 data shows that recently quenched galaxies become less common over time, with fast quenching dominating massive early galaxies and slow quenching later.
highlights: Fast‑quenching efficiency peaks in massive galaxies at z>1.5
Slow‑quenching efficiency rises below z≈1.5, shifting toward intermediate masses
Most recently quenched galaxies at z<0.5 inhabit low‑density environments
fRQGs retain disc‑like morphologies while sRQGs become more concentrated

genetic_code_break.headline: Genetic Code Breakthrough: Protist Reassigns Two Stop Codons to Different Amino Acids
genetic_code_break.summary: A newly identified freshwater ciliate rewrites two universal stop signals, TAA and TAG, to encode lysine and glutamic acid, challenging long‑held genetic code rules.
highlights: The organism Oligohymenophorea sp. PL0344 uses TAA for lysine and TAG for glutamic acid
Only TGA remains a conventional stop codon in this protist
Discovery published in PLOS Genetics (Oct 2023) after testing a single‑cell DNA sequencing method
Follow‑up work (Dec 2024) found similar codon reassignments in five other ciliates
Researchers involved Dr Jamie McGowan (Earlham Institute) and Prof Thomas Richards (University of Oxford)

6.headline: ALMA Detects Water, Methanol and Methyl Formate in HD 100546 and IRS 48 Disks
6.summary: ALMA band 5 observations reveal methanol‑rich IRS 48 with no water, while HD 100546 shows both water and methanol, yielding a comet‑like CH₃OH/H₂O ratio.
highlights: IRS 48 disk shows methanol detection but water vapor remains undetected, giving methanol‑to‑water column ratio >0.2.
HD 100546 disk contains water and methanol with CH₃OH/H₂O ≈0.02, matching the median cometary value.
Methyl formate‑to‑methanol ratio is ~0.2 in IRS 48 and ~2 in HD 100546, indicating chemical enhancement in the latter.
Non‑LTE analysis constrains optical depths and emitting regions of methanol lines in both disks.

einstein_probe_neutron_star_phase.headline: Einstein Probe Uncovers Hidden Ten‑Minute Soft X‑Ray Phase in Neutron Star Mergers
einstein_probe_neutron_star_phase.summary: A wide‑field soft X‑ray monitor detected nearly ten minutes of emission after a short gamma‑ray burst, revealing a previously missed merger phase.
highlights: Soft X‑ray emission persisted for ~10 minutes after the initial sub‑second gamma‑ray flash
The prolonged signal likely originates from a newly formed magnetar central engine
Multi‑wavelength follow‑up confirmed the event as a compact‑object merger, not a supernova
Einstein Probe’s wide‑field capability captured a phase missed by Swift BAT and similar missions

fastest_star_black_hole_spin.headline: Fastest Milky Way Star S301 Circles Black Hole, Offering Spin Clues
fastest_star_black_hole_spin.summary: Astronomers have identified star S301 orbiting Sagittarius A in an 8.7‑year, ultra‑eccentric path, enabling a direct probe of the black hole’s spin.
highlights: S301 completes an 8.7‑year orbit with eccentricity ≈ 0.98, bringing it within 1.78 billion km of Sagittarius A
At pericentre the star reaches ~25,000 km s⁻¹, the highest speed measured for any Milky Way star
Its orbit shows ~2° Schwarzschild precession per revolution and a detectable Lense‑Thirring wobble

buffalo_survey_subhalo_mass_function.headline: BUFFALO Survey Maps Subhalo Mass Function in Merging Cluster Abell 2744
buffalo_survey_subhalo_mass_function.summary: A combined strong‑ and weak‑lensing analysis using HST and JWST data reveals an excess of substructures in the massive cluster Abell 2744 (z = 0.308).
highlights: Strong‑lensing constraints and deep weak‑lensing imaging from HST and JWST were merged to map mass from core to outskirts
The derived subhalo mass function shows more detected subhalos than predicted by BAHAMAS ΛCDM simulations
The excess likely reflects Abell 2744’s highly disturbed dynamical state rather than new physics

dark_siren_cosmology_catalog_completenes.headline: Fainter Galaxies Barely Shift Dark Siren Cosmology in GWTC‑3 Study
dark_siren_cosmology_catalog_completenes.summary: A new analysis of GWTC‑3 events shows that adding dimmer galaxies from the GLADE+ catalog generally does not alter dark‑siren cosmological estimates, except for GW190814.
highlights: Including galaxies fainter than the standard magnitude cut has negligible impact on joint cosmological constraints for most
The well‑localized binary merger GW190814 shows a measurable shift when fainter galaxies overlap its redshift range.
Redshift distributions reveal that most dimmer galaxies lie beyond the distances of the majority of dark sirens.
Future deeper catalogs could make faint‑galaxy contributions significant for multi‑event analyses.

el_nino_temp_record_2026.headline: Central Pacific Ocean Hits Record 86°F, Hinting at Super El Niño
el_nino_temp_record_2026.summary: Sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region surpassed 86 °F (30 °C) for the first time, signaling an unprecedented warming episode.
highlights: Record‑breaking 86 °F (30 °C) observed in the Niño 3.4 zone
Anomaly now 6 °F (3.34 °C) above average, far exceeding typical El Niño peaks
Experts label the event a potential “super” El Niño driven by climate change
Forecasts suggest temperatures could reach 7.2 °F (4 °C) above average by November
Research links this extreme event to shifting patterns of central‑Pacific El Niños

gravitational_lenses_desi_2026.headline: AI uncovers 70 new gravitational lenses in massive DESI sky map
gravitational_lenses_desi_2026.summary: Using AI on the 5.6‑trillion‑pixel DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, an international team confirmed 70 new gravitational lenses, expanding the premier lens catalog.
highlights: 70 gravitational lenses were spectroscopically confirmed with VLT‑MUSE
The search employed a residual neural network on data from DECam, MzLS and BASS
The new lenses join the DESI Strong Lens Foundry, one of the largest confirmed samples

electronic_stripes_vortex.headline: Charge Stripes Reveal Majorana Modes in Iron‑Based Superconductor Vortices
electronic_stripes_vortex.summary: Using atomic‑scale scanning tunneling microscopy, researchers observed charge‑stripe patterns intensifying around vortex cores, one of which hosts a Majorana zero mode.
highlights: Charge stripes strengthen near vortex centers in Ba(Fe₀.₉₄Co₀.₀₆)₂As₂ thin films.
Two distinct vortex states were identified, one containing a Majorana zero mode.
Spectroscopic‑imaging STM revealed the spatial correlation between stripes and vortex bound states.

milky_way_simulation_2026_10_08.headline: Milky Way once a swarm of thousands of galaxies, new simulations show
milky_way_simulation_2026_10_08.summary: New supercomputer simulations reveal that in the first two billion years after the Big Bang, the Milky Way region hosted thousands of tiny galaxies that later merged into today’s single spiral.
highlights: The Megatron suite tracks gas, starlight and chemistry from 180 million to 2 billion years after the Big Bang
JWST observations of bright early galaxies and “Little Red Dots” challenge previous models
The simulation predicts distinct spectral signatures that can be directly compared with JWST data

mantle_flow_pacific_2026.headline: Fossilized Mantle Flow Traced Beneath Pacific’s Oldest Oceanic Plate
mantle_flow_pacific_2026.summary: Ocean-bottom seismometers reveal complex, ancient mantle flow patterns beneath the 160‑180 million‑year‑old Pacific Triangle, challenging simple plate‑motion models.
highlights: Seismic anisotropy shows spatially variable orientations not explained by present‑day plate motion alone
Oldest-1 ocean‑bottom seismometer array (2018‑2019) captured shear‑wave data across the Pacific Triangle
Mantle flow appears redirected around a sunken remnant of lithosphere and near the Magellan Seamount Trail

high_res_global_atmospheric_model.headline: Tokyo Researchers Achieve 220‑Meter Global Climate Model, Erasing Popcorn‑Rain Bias
high_res_global_atmospheric_model.summary: A University of Tokyo team built a 220‑meter global large‑eddy simulation that removes the artificial ‘popcorn‑like’ rain bias, improving extreme‑weather forecasts.
highlights: Resolution narrowed to 220 meters, about the length of two soccer fields
Simulation used nearly 1 trillion grid points and over half of the Fugaku supercomputer
Eliminated the long‑standing popcorn‑like rain bias in global storm‑resolving models

interpretation_of_nanohertz_gravitationa.headline: Cosmic Strings May Explain Nanohertz Gravitational Waves, Study Finds
interpretation_of_nanohertz_gravitationa.summary: A Bayesian analysis of NANOGrav and EPTA data suggests a brief post‑BBN matter and kination era could produce the observed nanohertz gravitational‑wave background.
highlights: Bayes factor of 3.63 supports a transient matter‑kination phase
Cosmic‑string tension remains essentially unchanged
Analysis uses NANOGrav 15‑year and EPTA DR2 New+ datasets
Result holds even if supermassive black‑hole binary contribution is small

2610_11435v1.headline: Δ Baryons Enable Faster Neutron Star Cooling via Direct Urca Processes
2610_11435v1.summary: Incorporating Δ direct Urca neutrino emission into simulations shows that these channels can markedly accelerate the thermal evolution of neutron stars.
highlights: Δ direct Urca processes provide an efficient neutrino‑cooling mechanism
Simulations reveal significantly lower surface temperatures for Δ‑admixed neutron stars
First systematic study of Δ baryon weak‑interaction channels in neutron star cooling

2610_11881v1.headline: LHAASO Detects Orbital Modulation of PeV Gamma Rays from Cygnus X‑3
2610_11881v1.summary: New LHAASO observations show ultrahigh‑energy gamma‑ray emission from Cygnus X‑3 that varies with the binary’s orbit, revealing wind‑regulated particle acceleration.
highlights: GeV emission arises from anisotropic inverse‑Compton scattering of stellar photons by relativistic electrons
Multi‑PeV protons escaping the inner jet produce TeV‑PeV gamma rays via photohadronic and hadronuclear interactions
A fast accretion‑driven disk wind currently shields escaping protons from the dense Wolf‑Rayet wind, suppressing PeV output

2610_11045v1.headline: Galaxy Clustering Offers New Way to Pinpoint Binary Black Hole Host Types
2610_11045v1.summary: A novel method uses galaxy clustering within gravitational‑wave localization zones to statistically infer whether binary black hole mergers occur in star‑forming or quenched galaxies.
highlights: Event‑level host likelihoods are built from neighboring galaxy counts around each merger detection
Forecasts for O5, post‑O5 and third‑generation detectors predict 90% lower credible limits of 0.19, 0.48 and 0.92 for the
The approach works without assuming specific formation efficiencies or merger delay‑time distributions

primordial_black_holes_as_a_natural_cons.headline: Scale‑Invariant U(1) Theory Links Thermal Inflation to Primordial Black Holes
primordial_black_holes_as_a_natural_cons.summary: A scale‑invariant U(1) gauge model with a nonminimal Higgs‑gravity coupling naturally generates large curvature perturbations that seed primordial black holes and associated gravitational‑wave signals.
highlights: Nonminimal gravitational interaction ξ ≈ O(1) gives the Higgs a Hubble‑scale negative mass‑squared term
Thermal fluctuations at the end of thermal inflation amplify curvature perturbations enough to form PBHs across a wide mass range
Resulting PBH population predicts correlated scalar‑induced and cosmic‑string gravitational waves detectable by pulsar timing

2610_11588v1.headline: New Method Reveals Radial Flows in Disc Galaxies Using 3DBarolo
2610_11588v1.summary: A novel 3DBarolo workflow quantifies axisymmetric radial motions in disc galaxies, overcoming warp degeneracy and offering insights into gas accretion processes.
highlights: Developed a dedicated 3DBarolo workflow to measure axisymmetric radial velocities
Validated the method with realistic mock galaxies and TNG50 simulated Milky Way‑like discs
Bootstrapping provides robust uncertainty estimates for radial flow measurements
Analysis of TNG50 galaxies shows widespread local inflows/outflows but no global coherent radial flow

ultrafast_core_level_spectroscopy_excito.institution: International collaboration (University of Glasgow, University of Tokyo, University of Sheffield, Kobe University)
ultrafast_core_level_spectroscopy_excito.headline: Ultrafast XUV Spectroscopy Captures Excitonic Precursors in 1T‑TiSe₂
ultrafast_core_level_spectroscopy_excito.summary: Using ultrafast broadband extreme‑ultraviolet absorption, researchers observed lingering excitonic correlations and heightened susceptibility near the 200 K transition in 1T‑TiSe₂.
highlights: UBXAS probed Se 4p and Ti 3d states with element‑specific resolution.
Excitonic response time scaled inversely with √laser fluence below 200 K.
Same fluence dependence persisted above the transition, indicating surviving excitonic interactions.
Near 200 K the response became ultra‑fast and fluence‑independent, revealing enhanced excitonic susceptibility.

molecular_movie_reveals_penicillin_synth.institution: University of Oxford and international collaborators
molecular_movie_reveals_penicillin_synth.headline: Oxford team captures molecular movie of penicillin biosynthesis
molecular_movie_reveals_penicillin_synth.summary: Using ultrafast XFEL snapshots, Oxford researchers revealed fleeting intermediates in penicillin’s β‑lactam ring formation, shedding light on antibiotic synthesis.
highlights: The enzyme isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS) was observed converting a linear peptide into the penicillin scaffold in real time
A thioaldehyde intermediate and a monocyclic β‑lactam intermediate were captured for the first time
Water molecules inside IPNS were shown to guide the reaction through precise proton transfers

2610_10741v1.headline: AI‑Driven 3D Gas Maps from Galaxy Surveys Enable Precise FRB Dispersion Measures
2610_10741v1.summary: A new generative model trained on the CAMELS50 simulation reconstructs three‑dimensional cosmic baryon density, improving FRB dispersion‑measure predictions across large volumes.
highlights: Model conditions on stellar‑mass weighted galaxy density, cosmological parameters, and baryon suppression power spectrum
Validated on test boxes, matching true DM per sightline and overall distribution
Scales to volumes ~4³ times larger than training, covering typical FRB cosmological paths
Provides a route to constrain feedback models using FRBs, X‑ray, SZ effect, and weak‑lensing

light_readout_mof_spin.institution: University of Glasgow (with partners University of Tokyo, University of Sheffield, Kobe University)
light_readout_mof_spin.headline: Light Reads Electron Spins in MOFs, Paving Way for Quantum Chemical Sensors
light_readout_mof_spin.summary: Researchers used optically detected magnetic resonance to read electron spin states inside a porous metal‑organic framework, opening a route to ultra‑sensitive quantum sensors.
highlights: First optical readout of spin resonance in a metal‑organic framework
Collaboration spans University of Glasgow, University of Tokyo, University of Sheffield and Kobe University
Technique could enable molecular‑scale detection of chemicals via a "quantum nose"

hidden_in_between_materials_for_batterie.headline: Hidden Intermediate Phases Reveal New β‑BiVO₄ Form for Solar Fuels and Batteries
hidden_in_between_materials_for_batterie.summary: Researchers at the University of Warwick uncovered transient material phases during heating, discovering a kinetic β‑BiVO₄ polymorph with a larger band gap and a lithium‑rich intermediate promising advances in solar‑fuel production and next‑generation
highlights: β‑BiVO₄ exhibits a distinct atomic arrangement and significantly larger band gap than known BiVO₄ forms
A lithium‑rich intermediate phase demonstrated high lithium storage capacity, hinting at battery applications
The study employed solid‑state NMR, X‑ray diffraction, and pair distribution function analysis to capture fleeting intermediates

bacteria_turn_a_virus_own_weapon_against.headline: Bacterial Immune System Uses Viral Enzyme to Trigger Self-Destruct Response
bacteria_turn_a_virus_own_weapon_against.summary: Scientists discovered that phage‑produced proteases cleave a bacterial CBASS sensor, activating a lethal suicide pathway that halts viral spread.
highlights: The viral protease cuts the bacterial sensor protein, acting as the alarm signal.
Activation of CBASS triggers an extreme “last‑resort” suicide response in the infected bacterium.
CBASS shares ancestry with a human immune pathway, indicating billions‑year evolutionary conservation.
Findings published in Science (2026) may improve phage‑therapy design against antibiotic‑resistant infections.

variable_water_clouds_jwst.headline: James Webb Telescope Captures Variable Water Clouds on Nearby Brown Dwarf
variable_water_clouds_jwst.summary: Using JWST, astronomers recorded the first real‑time changes in water‑cloud thickness on the cold brown dwarf WISE 0855, 7.5 light‑years away.
highlights: Water clouds on WISE 0855 thicken and thin as the object rotates
Carbon monoxide and phosphine signals reveal deep convective mixing
JWST’s medium‑resolution spectrograph delivered the most detailed time‑series portrait of a sub‑stellar atmosphere

frb_jwst_origin.headline: Young Galaxy Magnetar Powers Most Distant Fast Radio Burst Yet Seen
frb_jwst_origin.summary: A faint galaxy observed by JWST at 3 billion years old hosts FRB 20240304B, supporting a magnetar origin over neutron‑star mergers.
highlights: MeerKAT radio array precisely localized FRB 20240304B
JWST identified a small host galaxy at a cosmic age of ~3 billion years
Spectroscopy shows the galaxy’s stars formed within ~30 million years
The young stellar environment favors a magnetar over a neutron‑star merger origin
Findings are reported in arXiv preprint arXiv:2508.01648 (2025)

tiny_marine_microbe.headline: Tiny marine archaeon Candidatus Sukunaarchaeum mirabile boasts the smallest known genome yet retains full
tiny_marine_microbe.summary: Researchers uncovered the ultra‑reduced archaeon Candidatus Sukunaarchaeum mirabile, with just 189 protein‑coding genes, that still copies its DNA and makes proteins despite lacking nutrient‑production genes.
highlights: Genome size is less than half that of the smallest previously known archaeal genome
Contains only 189 protein‑coding genes yet retains DNA‑replication and protein‑synthesis pathways
Lacks genes for nutrient and energy production, suggesting reliance on a host or partner

quantum_chip_multi_photon_memory.institution: University of California, Santa Barbara (or similar)
quantum_chip_multi_photon_memory.headline: Quantum Chip Stores Multiple Photons for Over 1 Microsecond, Paving Way for Scalable Memory
quantum_chip_multi_photon_memory.summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana‑Champaign demonstrated a thin‑film lithium niobate chip that holds several photons simultaneously for more than a microsecond, a key step toward practical quantum memory.
highlights: Integrated nanophotonic platform uses erbium‑doped thin‑film lithium niobate
Atomic frequency comb technique enables multi‑photon storage exceeding 1 μs
Device shows high‑fidelity quantum information preservation and potential wafer‑scale manufacturing

fish_genes_urban.headline: Urban Coastal Waters Feed Fish but Trigger Hidden Genetic Stress
fish_genes_urban.summary: Blue damselfish thriving near Okinawa’s urban coastlines show abundant nutrition yet exhibit genome-wide stress signatures indicating chronic physiological strain.
highlights: Researchers sampled blue damselfish from 18 sites spanning pristine to heavily urbanized reefs in Okinawa
Genome-wide analysis identified 425 juvenile and 585 adult liver genes linked to urbanization
Urban fish displayed gene patterns similar to well‑fed lab fish but with heightened inflammatory responses
The study proposes a “junk food effect” where abundant food comes at a physiological cost

fast_two_photon_imaging.headline: Cornell Team Unveils Faster Two‑Photon Fluorescence Polarization Microscopy for Real‑Time Metabolism
fast_two_photon_imaging.summary: Researchers at Cornell have created a rapid two‑photon fluorescence polarization method that tracks NAD(P)H metabolism in live cells with minimal light exposure.
highlights: New two‑photon fluorescence polarization ratiometric microscopy (FPRM) reduces imaging time and light dose compared to
Polarization readout distinguishes protein‑bound versus free NAD(P)H, revealing cellular energy states instantly.
The technique works in three‑dimensional organoids, enabling dynamic metabolic studies in tissue‑like environments.

lunar_cave_mission.headline: NASA’s GIMLI Mission to Probe Lunar Pit for Hidden Lava Tube
lunar_cave_mission.summary: The GIMLI probe will map the Marius Hills Pit in Oceanus Procellarum, seeking the first on‑site evidence of a subsurface lunar lava tube.
highlights: GIMLI will deploy ground‑penetrating radar, a gravimeter, and seismic sensors to detect voids beneath the pit.
Mission led by the Planetary Science Institute with PI Than Putzig and built by Honeybee Robotics (Blue Origin).
A confirmed lava tube could shield future astronauts from radiation, micrometeoroids, and extreme temperature swings.
The project is funded through NASA’s PRISM program and will launch via the Commercial Lunar Payload Services partnership.

stratospheric_balloon_telescope_sunrise3.headline: SUNRISE III Balloon Telescope Uncovers Hidden Magnetic Threads in the Quiet Sun
stratospheric_balloon_telescope_sunrise3.summary: A 1 m solar telescope lifted to 35 km by a helium balloon revealed narrow 725 km magnetic threads with 10‑20 Gauss fields and opposite‑polarity intrusions in the quiet‑Sun chromosphere.
highlights: SUNRISE III used the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared spectroPolarimeter (SCIP) to map full‑Stokes polarimetry of the solar
The observed magnetic threads are 725 km wide, with field strengths fluctuating between 10 and 20 Gauss, and show
MURaM‑ChE simulations reproduced these intrusions as twisted flux ropes 2,000‑7,000 km long
Magnetic field strength rises to ~40 Gauss above the solar limb, suggesting measurement differences due to spicule density

plastic_chemical_ovary.headline: Common Plastic Chemical DEHP Disrupts Multiple Human Ovarian Cell Types
plastic_chemical_ovary.summary: New eBioMedicine study shows that DEHP metabolite MEHP alters gene expression across diverse ovarian cells, including sensitive glial cells, at realistic exposure levels.
highlights: MEHP exposure changed expression of thousands of genes in seven ovarian cell types
Glial cells in the ovary were unusually sensitive to even low‑dose MEHP
Dose‑dependent effects were observed at 20.51 nM, an epidemiologically relevant concentration

type5_diabetes.headline: IDF Officially Recognizes Type 5 Diabetes, a Malnutrition‑Related Form
type5_diabetes.summary: The International Diabetes Federation’s 2025 decision names a fifth diabetes type linked to chronic nutrient deficiency, affecting up to 25 million people worldwide.
highlights: Type 5 diabetes, formerly MRDM, is estimated to affect up to 25 million people, mainly in low‑ and middle‑income regions.
The IDF created a working group in 2025 chaired by Meredith Hawkins to draft diagnostic criteria and treatment guidelines.
Studies show patients have insulin deficiency but retain insulin sensitivity, distinguishing them from Types 1 and 2 diabetes.
Existing insulin therapies can cause dangerous hypoglycemia in malnourished patients, prompting calls for tailored treatment.

4.headline: Chandra Reveals Kiloparsec-Scale Jet at Record-Breaking z=6.1
4.summary: Deep 360 ks Chandra observations resolve the distant AGN jet into two X‑ray components, showing a steep photon index and an 18% extended‑to‑core luminosity ratio.
highlights: Extended X‑ray emission splits into two slightly resolved components
Photon index of the jet is Γ = 2.25, steeper than the core’s Γ = 1.86
Extended‑to‑core luminosity ratio reaches 18%
Simulations suggest an AXIS‑like mission could boost photon counts by ~17×

1.headline: Hidden POLO Pathway Discovered: Eye’s New Lymphatic Drainage System
1.summary: Scientists at UBC and the University of Toronto identified a posterior ocular lymphatic outflow (POLO) in mice that clears fluid and waste from the retina, reshaping blindness research.
highlights: POLO pathway routes fluid from the choroid to orbital lymph nodes
Discovery challenges a century‑old view that the eye lacks lymphatics
Potential target for glaucoma and macular degeneration therapies
Study published in Translational Vision Science & Technology

cannabis_anxiety_brain_cells.headline: Cannabis Triggers Anxiety via Activation of Central Amygdala Somatostatin Neurons
